target/tests/test_subtract.py wraps its assertion in try/except Exception: pass. The test can't fail on a wrong result, because AssertionError is an Exception and gets swallowed. It would pass against the buggy multiplication implementation, so it doesn't verify anything and effectively bypasses testing.

The test has only one case, subtract(3, 1). Even without the try/except, that case can't distinguish subtraction from other operations. For example, 3 - 1 and 3 // 1 + ... style mistakes could pass, and there are no negative or zero cases.
